purpose: Rater calibration (Docs/v1.3/human-labelling-protocol.md section 5). Open only after both raters have answered every row. Not counted in any agreement figure.
renderedWith: claimText() and excerpt() of scripts/v1.3/lib/labelling/meaningful-prompt.ts (comments stripped by excerpt-scrub.ts); decoy claims written in the same wording as the tool messages

items.why: A domain entity takes an HTTP framework type: `fromRequest(request: Request)` puts the web framework into the entity's API (Martin 2017 ch. 22 and ch. 32). The import is type-only; whether a type-only import counts is construct question Q2 (open), but here the entity's own signature is framework-shaped, so the meaningful answer is yes under either reading. Tool and both manifests agree.
Strict layering (Fowler 2002 ch. 1; POSA 1996, Layers): presentation must reach persistence through the business layer. Tool, author-manifest and blind manifest all agree.

An advisory metric on the CLEAN variant. A controller in the outermost circle is meant to be unstable (it depends on use cases and nothing depends on it). Neither manifest expects anything here. Teaches: a measured number is not a defect, and outer-layer instability is by design.

A domain entity imports an application-layer command: the dependency points outward from the domain (Evans 2003 ch. 4). Tool and both manifests agree. The import is type-only (construct question Q2); the domain still names an application type in its code, so the meaningful answer stays yes.

A file cycle between two domain-model files inside one layer. ADP (Martin 2017 ch. 14) is stated for components, not files, so whether an in-layer file cycle is a violation is construct question Q3, open and marked high-stakes. Discuss both readings; neither answer is wrong at calibration.

Decoy on the CLEAN layered variant. Presentation calling the layer directly below it is exactly what layering prescribes. A neutral claim can sound like a finding; the rater must check it against the style, not against its tone.
A domain service imports a concrete infrastructure clock: the Dependency Rule (Martin 2017 ch. 22) is broken. Tool and both manifests agree.

The repository no longer declares `implements` for the domain-owned port, but TypeScript's structural typing still lets it be passed where the port is expected, so the inversion holds at run time. Both manifests expect the finding; construct question Q9 (missing implements under structural typing) asks whether the missing declaration alone is the defect.

A NEAR-MISS variant. Hexagonal architecture does not define strict layering: an inbound adapter may use a domain value type that its port speaks (Cockburn 2005). The tool is silent here (layer skipping is advisory and not raised); the author-manifest expects nothing; the blind manifest noted an advisory skip only. Teaches: do not import the strict-layering reading into hexagonal.

A repository implementation maps entities to an HTTP response DTO. Under a Clean reading, infrastructure depending on an application-side DTO points inward and the Dependency Rule allows it; under the NestJS preset's layer order the edge runs against the allowed direction, which is construct question Q13 (layer order, RDQ-2). Either way a repository that shapes API responses mixes persistence and presentation, so many architects would want it changed. Tool and both manifests flag it; the rule it belongs to is the open part.
